THE FIX: authoredCount now reads authored.size — the count of records in the /interactions store (already loaded and passed in), which is what the panel hint 'records in /interactions/' has always promised. missingCount stays pairs.filter(p => !p.authored).length and each pair's authored flag/type is still read from the store, so even a stale queue that still listed an authored pair would render it 'authored' and exclude it from the missing tally (robust to queue staleness). No analyzer/gap-planner change: interaction_coverage already counts authored records and already prunes authored pairs from the queue. VALIDATOR: the naming/schema gate the issue asks for already exists — tools/validate.ts pass 14 (added with D-057) compiles interaction.schema.json, validates every /interactions/*.json, and cross-checks pair sorted + distinct, both ids in the registry roster, filename = {pair[0]}__{pair[1]}.json, and no pair authored twice; a single-vs-double-underscore filename, a reversed FR-11/SP-08 order, or a schema-invalid record fails CI rather than being silently skipped by the app reader (which catches-and-skips by design because the validator is the gate). lib/types.ts unchanged. Verify: /maturation now shows AUTHORED 1 with the FR-11×SP-08 record present, the missing-pairs list unchanged (the pair stays absent because it is covered), and interaction_coverage on the entry cells reflecting the record; npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Interaction batch 1 authored — 10 pairs gating the four zero-coverage packs
decisions.body: First owner-authored batch of pairwise interaction records (D-057) landed in /interactions: EN-03__VR-02, EN-03__ZE-07, VR-02__ZE-07, CG-05__FR-11, CG-05__RE-10, CG-05__SP-08, FR-11__RE-10, ID-12__VR-02, EN-03__ST-09, LA-01__ST-09 — committed verbatim (texts, grades, source lines unmodified). decisions.title: Mechanism ids carry their L0 node in the UI so perception (S7) is distinguishable from motivational mechanisms
decisions.body: S7 Perception & comprehension (cross_cutting: true, D-062) reads and renders as the seventh L0 node on /registry with its six candidate stubs (PS-13, CL-14, MM-15, PF-16, SC-17, IF-18) — computeRegistryTree already maps all taxonomy nodes with no S1–S6 cap, so no fix was needed there; likewise the six S7 stubs (incl. PS-13) were already present in the /ops evidence target list via loadSeedStubs and in corpora/_ops/connectors/evidence.json. THE GAP was that bare mechanism ids gave the operator no way to tell a cross-cutting perception mechanism from a motivational one. THE POLICY: a single computed index resolves every mechanism id to its L0 parent, and the id is never shown alone where the parent matters. lib/status.ts adds MechanismNodeRef + loadMechanismNodeIndex() — reads registry/taxonomy.json + full records + seed stubs (never hardcoded), mapping each id to { parent, parentName, crossCutting } where crossCutting = the L0 node's flag OR the record's own. /ops target picker: the flat, unlabeled datalist/select/chips are replaced by node-grouped UI (app/ops/ops-client.tsx groupIdsByNode + nodeHeading) — the 'what it harvests' chips are grouped under node headings (S1–S6 motivational, S7 cross-cutting amber-tagged), the add-target control is a <select> with <optgroup> per node, and the run-target <select> is likewise grouped; a hand-typed id not in the registry falls into a trailing 'not in registry' group rather than being dropped. /maturation: the harvest queue rows and interaction-authoring pair rows render a NodeBadge after each bare mechanism id (parent id + amber 'cross-cutting' marker, full node name on hover). The matrix hover and pack-export panel show pack ids (not mechanism ids) and the cross-cutting perception row is already its own labelled row group (D-067), so they needed no change. No status literal added (honesty rule, .cursorrules #2); every label is computed from files. Verify: /registry shows S7 as the 7th node with 6 stubs + cross-cutting tag; /ops target picker groups all mechanisms under node headings with all six S7 ids present; /maturation queue and interaction pairs show the parent node on each id; npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: SC-17 and IF-18 evidence_terms corrected for polysemy; a poisoned corpus is cleared before re-harvest so the connector's first-harvest path handles a replacement, not a D-038 regression
decisions.body: The first S7 candidate harvests (D-063) produced two poisoned corpora: SC-17 'Scanning & visual attention' collided with scanning/scintigraphy microscopy and web servers (its top foundational works were SILAC proteomics, the FoldX web server, X-ray diffraction microscopy), and IF-18 'Information foraging' collided with ecological foraging and economics search costs (top works were fractional Brownian motion, agricultural economics, livestock climate). Root cause is term polysemy, not a connector bug — tools/connectors/evidence.ts resolves terms from the record's evidence_terms (D-015) and the generic terms matched the wrong literatures. FIX (owner-provided terms, rule 8 — no invented science, only search strings): registry/mechanisms/_seed/SC-17.json evidence_terms -> [visual attention web page; eye movements reading screen; banner blindness advertising; web page fixation attention advertisement; visual hierarchy attention interface; attention capture web design]; registry/mechanisms/_seed/IF-18.json evidence_terms -> [information foraging theory Pirolli; information scent user navigation; information scent hypertext browsing; web navigation cue judgment; information seeking behaviour interface]. pinned_evidence left untouched. THE GUARD INTERACTION: the corrected terms are narrower, so a re-harvest yields fewer records than the polluted corpora (SC-17 298, IF-18 316) and would trip the anti-regression guard (D-038, evidence.ts): the run would write {id}.regression.json and KEEP the bad file. That guard is correct — it cannot tell a genuine regression from an intentional replacement of a poisoned corpus. THE MECHANISM (no code change, no new machinery): the poisoned corpus files (corpora/evidence/SC-17.json, IF-18.json) and their stale digests were DELETED before re-running, so the connector took its first-harvest path (previousRecords === null): the D-038 regression guard is skipped and the D-058 novelty gate reports novelty 1 (full novelty, not a low-novelty re-read of the canon). The seed stubs are candidate with dossier_ref absent, so the D-038 validation hard rule (a dossier'd record must carry evidence_terms) does not apply and validate stays green. RESULT after re-harvest: SC-17 307 records (was 298), novelty 1 (305/305 new), category_counts foundational 3 / meta-analysis 6 / replication 24 / dissent 87 / recent 111 — foundational now led by 'Attention web designers: You have 50 milliseconds to make a good first impression!' (Behavior & Information Technology, 1073 cites) with 'WHY DO PEOPLE AVOID ADVERTISING ON THE INTERNET?' (banner blindness) prominent; ~197/307 records HCI vs ~7 off-domain. IF-18 175 records, novelty 1 (175/175 new), foundational 1 / meta-analysis 2 / replication 9 / dissent 53 / recent 58 — the Pirolli & Card pin resolved via OpenAlex (1263 cites, foundational) and the corpus is led by Information Foraging, SNIF-ACT, Scented Widgets, and 'The scent of a site'; ~100/175 HCI vs ~3 off-domain. Both runs returned status partial with warnings.capped: the keyless Semantic Scholar pool 429'd persistently and the D-027 retry/backoff passes consumed the max_calls_per_run=150 _ops budget (a graceful stop, not a failure); SC-17's two pins fell back to owner-provided metadata (D-017) because the budget was spent before the pin lookups. The residual off-domain tail (~2% of each corpus) comes from the D-058 generic contrast-angle suffixes (cross-domain generalization, boundary conditions), not from the polysemy — a known diversity-vs-precision trade-off, not a re-harvest defect. The proteomics/microscopy/ecology/agriculture domination is gone: both corpora are now human-attention / HCI literature.

decisions.title: S7 batch 1 (CL-14, MM-15, PS-13, PF-16) admitted to incubating; SC-17 and IF-18 held for re-harvest after term collision
decisions.body: The first four S7 Perception & comprehension mechanisms passed the dossier gate (SPEC §3.3: total >= 11 with evidence >= 2 and safety >= 2) and were promoted from the temp staging folder to full L1 records — CL-14 Cognitive load, MM-15 Multimedia design principles, PS-13, PF-16 Processing fluency — each cross_cutting: true, parent S7, lifecycle_status incubating, verdict incubating. Owner-authored content (texts, evidence grades, axis scores, dissent statements) was committed VERBATIM (.cursorrules rule 8): the four full records moved to registry/mechanisms/{id}.json (replacing and deleting their _seed/{id}.json candidate stubs so the roster carries one entry per id), and the four dossiers moved to dossiers/{id}.json. PF-16 is admitted at the total-11 admission FLOOR by design: safety 1 is the lowest score in S7 and among the lowest in the registry because the mechanism includes the illusory-truth effect (repeated/fluent claims judged more accurate irrespective of accuracy; Fazio et al. 2015 showed prior knowledge does not protect) — the cognitive basis of misinformation — and it is constrained by three block-severity guardrails (no fluency on unsupported claims; no deliberate disfluency to obstruct; material information at least as fluent as promotional content). This is the honest position, preserved as written, not a scoring error. PS-13's dossier carries an owner note recommending a re-harvest before any CORE promotion; preserved as written. SC-17 Scanning & visual attention and IF-18 Information foraging remain candidate seed stubs, HELD for re-harvest: their first harvests were poisoned by term polysemy and their evidence_terms were corrected but the corpora not yet re-validated for a gate (D-072). RESULT: registry now shows S7 with 4 full records + 2 candidates; 16 full mechanism records and 16 dossiers on file. render-cards emitted cards/{CL-14,MM-15,PS-13,PF-16}.md; render-packs (D-066) now finds four full records whose L0 parent (S7) is cross_cutting and emits them into the cross_cutting_perception section of EVERY generated pack (previously the honest empty [] placeholder), and the export bundle regenerated. npm run validate green (full records + seedStub, dossier totals equal axis sums, D-019 non-empty dissent on all four corpora, roster cross-references); npm run build green.

decisions.title: S7 perception node complete — six cross-cutting mechanisms admitted to incubating
