decisions.title: Proposal realization-cl-14-progressive-disclosure-of-advanced-f-7a339e24183c rejected
decisions.body: Owner owner rejected realization proposal realization-cl-14-progressive-disclosure-of-advanced-f-7a339e24183c for CL-14. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Mis-anchored. Expertise reversal states that SUPPORT harms EXPERTS; this pattern withholds advanced FEATURES from NOVICES, which runs the effect backwards. Hiding complexity from a beginner is justified by general cognitive load, not by cl-14-002, and its only quote is the effect's own sentence, so nothing in its evidence half supports the direction it takes. If it returns it must anchor to a CL-14 load effect, not to expertise reversal.

decisions.title: Envelope confidence is corrected inside the decision transaction, never by hand in git
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the edit action replaced payload and nothing else, so an owner who judged the pipeline's confidence unearned had two options: leave a number they disbelieved, or open the proposal file and change it in a separate commit. The second is what happened, and it breaks the one property the transaction exists to hold. D-113 requires a reason on every decision, and a hand-edited file carries no reason, no actor and no decision id — the corrected number becomes exactly as unexplained as the asserted one it replaced, and cl-14-002's regrade only reads as justified because the grade travelled with the payload while its confidence did not. DECISION: ProposalDecisionRequest gains an optional editedConfidence, applied to the envelope in the same atomic transaction as editedPayload, exposed as --confidence on the proposal CLI. Refused on approve and reject: the payload an approval commits is the one that was reviewed, and a number changed at approval time was reviewed by nobody. Refused outside [0,1] with the flag named in the message rather than a JSON Schema path, because a nonsense value should blame the input that carried it. Omitting the flag leaves the existing number untouched, so absent and corrected stay distinguishable. The confidence FLOOR is unchanged and still an extraction-time gate — an owner may set a value below it, since a held proposal and an owner-corrected low confidence are different facts. /review keeps its payload-only edit form; adding a confidence field to the UI would be a knowledge-editing surface the constitution does not allow, and the CLI is the recovery path the library already documents.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-modality-effect-c16093817de1 rejected
decisions.body: Owner owner rejected effect proposal effect-cl-14-modality-effect-c16093817de1 for CL-14. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Inverted. The sole cited paper (Tabbers, Martens & van Merrienboer 2004) found the OPPOSITE of this fact. The quoted span at offsets 369-638 sits in the abstract's BACKGROUND section, where the paper restates what cognitive load theory and Mayer's theory PREDICT. Its own RESULTS report that replacing visual text with spoken text produced LOWER retention and transfer scores, and CONCLUSIONS names the finding 'a reverse modality effect', attributed to the instructions being learner-paced rather than system-paced. The model quoted the paper accurately, from the part of the paper the paper went on to refute. This is not a weak effect to be downgraded: an effect whose only source reports its reversal is evidence against, and filing it at any grade would put a false claim in the registry under a humble-looking label. Approving the reverse effect instead would need a fresh extraction anchored to the RESULTS span, not an edit of this one.

decisions.title: For effects and realizations, an edited payload's provenance is the envelope's provenance
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: found while executing the two CL-14 edits the owner ordered. effect.schema.json and the proposal envelope require payload.provenance and envelope provenance to be EXACTLY EQUAL (assertPayloadProvenance), and the edit action replaces payload only. The two are therefore jointly unsatisfiable for any edit that touches provenance: dropping a mis-anchored citation, or re-anchoring a quote to a different span of the same record, fails an equality check the edit has no way to reach. That is not a narrow inconvenience — the two commonest owner corrections on an extraction-authored proposal are 'this citation is not evidence' and 'this quote is from the wrong part of the paper', and neither was expressible. The only routes left were to reject a proposal that was substantially right, or to hand-edit the file in git, which is precisely what D-122 closed. DECISION: for effect and realization, the two types whose schema declares the equality, the envelope provenance is a PROJECTION of the payload's and an edit carries it up automatically. Every other type keeps an independently authored envelope: dossier axis provenance is a SUBSET of the envelope rather than equal to it, so mirroring there would silently widen what the envelope claims. This cannot mask a divergence, because the proposal as read on disk is checked for one before the edit is applied, and the mirrored provenance is re-grounded against the corpus by assertResolvableProvenance — including span re-slicing and hash verification under D-110 — before any artifact is projected. What an owner still cannot do is invent provenance: a re-anchored span must resolve in the corpus, so the edit can move a quote to another part of a cited record but not to a record the pipeline never read.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-cueing-effect-01aaa2ec2e72 edited
decisions.body: Owner owner edited effect proposal effect-cl-14-cueing-effect-01aaa2ec2e72 for CL-14. The validated proposal payload was updated for further review. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Gutted to what the paper actually found, and kept rather than rejected. The direction survives contact with the data: the paper's RESULTS report that adding visual cues raised retention scores, which points the same way as the proposal — unlike the modality half, which reversed. What does not survive is the magnitude and the generality, so the fact now says the study found only a weak cueing effect that does not easily generalise beyond the laboratory, and the boundary names the learner-paced non-laboratory setting where that was observed. Both provenance items are now findings spans (RESULTS 1190-1260, CONCLUSIONS 1369-1527) on the same record; the model's original BACKGROUND span at 434-638, which restated theory the paper went on to qualify, is gone. Grade B+ to C, confidence 0.85 to 0.55. Kept rather than rejected for two reasons: a weak positive with a named boundary is usable by a generator as a constraint — do not spend design budget on cueing as a primary lever — and an empty queue invites the next extraction run to re-propose cueing at B+ from the same BACKGROUND sentence.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-cueing-effect-01aaa2ec2e72 approved
decisions.body: Owner owner approved effect proposal effect-cl-14-cueing-effect-01aaa2ec2e72 for CL-14. The validated proposal status and authoritative projection were committed atomically. Reason: Accepted at C after the re-anchoring in D-125. What is being filed is a weak positive with a named boundary, not a robust effect: one classroom study, cues raised retention but not transfer, and the authors themselves call the cueing effect weak and say it does not easily generalise beyond the laboratory. A generator should read this as a reason NOT to treat cueing as a primary lever, and as the boundary that a future proposal claiming a strong cueing effect has to argue past. Both citations are findings spans on the same DOI, so the record is consistent with the span_role gate rather than grandfathered against it.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654 edited
decisions.body: Owner owner edited effect proposal effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654 for CL-14. The validated proposal payload was updated for further review. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Narrowed to the evidence that survives. Three changes. (1) The clause 'which increases extraneous working memory load' is gone: it appears in no cited span. It comes from the Ayres and Sweller chapter's theoretical rationale, and the model welded it onto a sentence from a different paper. (2) The second citation is dropped from provenance AND from source. Its span states a design prescription -- 'it is important to avoid formats that require learners to split their attention' -- which is what an instructional designer SHOULD do, not what a study FOUND. A prescription cannot be evidence for a phenomenon. (3) Grade A to C+, confidence 0.95 to 0.7, because one DOI remains and a single-record basis is capped below the A band. Added, beyond the literal narrowing: a second span on the SAME record at 871-925, 'The results of 6 experiments supported this hypothesis'. The surviving 314-469 span is the paper's own premise -- the abstract says 'The logic was based on the split-attention effect' -- so on its own this record is exactly what the span_role gate exists to drop. The 871-925 span is the paper's finding that the prediction built on that premise held. With both, the record rests on a premise the paper went on to confirm rather than on a premise nobody checked, and it survives the gate instead of being grandfathered past it.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654 approved
decisions.body: Owner owner approved effect proposal effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654 for CL-14. The validated proposal status and authoritative projection were committed atomically. Reason: Approved at C+ after the narrowing in D-127. This is the first CL-14 effect resting on a primary experimental paper rather than a review, and it is still capped in the C band because the corpus holds exactly one DOI for it -- the split-attention literature is far larger than our corpus of it, and the grade states what WE hold, not what the field holds. The record is deliberately less than the model claimed: no extraneous-load mechanism, no second source, no A.

decisions.title: A span must declare what it is DOING in its source, and only a finding can ground a fact
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the first extraction run produced three effect proposals. Two of them quoted a BACKGROUND premise as though the cited study had found it, and one of those papers (Tabbers, Martens & van Merrienboer 2004) went on to report the OPPOSITE — its own CONCLUSIONS section names 'a reverse modality effect'. Every quote was verbatim, every span re-sliced, every hash matched. D-110 was working perfectly and had nothing to say, because the defect was not in the text but in the text's ROLE: a paper is not one voice, and 'replacing visual text with spoken text ... increase[s] the effectiveness of multimedia instructions' is what cognitive load theory PREDICTS, restated by a paper whose data refuted it. Grounding proves the words are the source's. It cannot prove the source was asserting them. DECISION: every extraction-authored citation asserts span_role from a closed vocabulary — background, hypothesis, method, finding, limitation — and the assertion is then ARGUED WITH, using the source text alone, in lib/span-role.ts. (1) STRUCTURE: when an abstract labels its own sections, the label constrains the role; a span inside BACKGROUND or METHOD cannot be this paper's finding. Labels are matched against a closed vocabulary, so the DOI:, ORCID:, ISBN: and STOP-IT: headings that also appear before colons in this corpus create no sections. (2) DOWNSTREAM CONTRADICTION: a span asserted as a finding, followed in the same text by a sentence that reverses it AND shares at least three distinctive words with it, is a premise the paper overturned. Skipped when the span itself carries a reversal marker, because a quote that states the qualification cannot be undone by it — without that rule the honest quote 'Only a weak cueing effect and even a reverse modality effect have been found' would be refused for being followed by the sentence explaining it. (3) THE FINDING REQUIREMENT is a property of the ITEM, not of a citation: at least one citation must be a finding, but an item may cite the premise its finding confirms — which is the shape cl-14-001 was narrowed to in D-127, where the paper's own 'The logic was based on the split-attention effect' sits beside 'The results of 6 experiments supported this hypothesis'. Requiring every citation to be a finding would have forbidden the most honest record in the repo. MEASURED, not asserted: across 3192 abstracts in the evidence corpora, only 3.8% carry two or more recognised section labels, so the structural check is silent on 96% and the downstream check is the workhorse there. A probe quoting the OPENING 200 characters and claiming a finding is refused 6.1% of the time (3.1% structural, 3.1% downstream); a probe quoting the LAST 200 characters, where results and conclusions live, is admitted 99.8% of the time, and every one of the six refusals is a full-text record whose tail genuinely sits in a Method, Rationale or Context section. Zero downstream false positives on findings-region text. The one spurious marker found while measuring — 'reverse-engineering' read as a reversal — is excluded by name. PERSISTED, not merely checked: span_role travels on the provenance item through the ledger, the extract-to-synthesize round trip, the proposal and the approved record, because a reader asking why an effect is graded as it is needs to see that a citation is the paper's result rather than its opening premise, and re-deriving that would mean re-reading the source with the same judgement that was already made. ENFORCEMENT follows the D-110 pattern — optional in the three schemas, required in code — with one addition D-110 did not need: a cutoff. D-110 preceded any extraction output; span_role arrives after eight items are already committed, and there is NO BACKFILL, because a role invented now for a span a model read last week would be my judgement wearing the pipeline's authority, which is the exact substitution this field exists to prevent. So requiresSpanRole() checks proposed_at against SPAN_ROLE_REQUIRED_FROM, and tools/validate.ts prints the roleless remainder every run so it cannot quietly become permanent. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CATCH, stated because the next failure will come from here: an unstructured abstract whose premise nothing downstream contradicts. Mousavi, Low & Sweller 1995 is exactly that case — 'The split-attention effect occurs when students must split their attention' is the paper's premise, the abstract has no section labels, and the paper CONFIRMS the premise rather than reversing it. Nothing in this decision would stop a model that labels it 'finding'. The only defence there is the model's own honesty and the owner's reading, which is why the gate is a floor and not a ceiling. COST: a candidate wrongly refused is recoverable — the owner can hand-author the record, or edit a proposal under D-124 — while a false fact filed at any grade is not. The gate is set to refuse on doubt for that reason, and every refusal records the section label or the matched marker with its shared words, so a wrong refusal is arguable rather than mysterious.
